findings.title: Self-service password reset dead-ends: the email link lands on a page that cannot complete the reset
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:327-330 — forgot-password sends Supabase resetPasswordForEmail with redirectTo `<APP_BASE_URL>/password-reset` (GoTrue appends a PKCE `code` or recovery token to that URL)
apps/web/app/(public)/password-reset/page.tsx:1-37 — the page is client-only, reads no searchParams/hash, and posts email + new password directly
apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:349-378 — POST /api/v1/auth/reset-password is guarded by requireAuth and rejects any email != req.authUser.email, so it only works for an already-signed-in user
apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts:8-15 — the only route that exchanges a Supabase `code` into a session is /auth/callback, which the reset email never targets
grep 'searchParams|useSearchParams|location.hash' apps/web/app/(public)/password-reset/page.tsx → 0 matches
findings.impact: A user who forgets their password can never recover access from the emailed link; the reset form returns an auth error (or nothing useful), so every reset escalates to manual admin intervention. The profile-page password change uses the same endpoint, which is why the flow appears to work for signed-in users.
findings.recommendation: Route the reset link through /auth/callback (or have /password-reset read the `code`/fragment, exchange it, then call reset-password with the resulting session). Add an E2E test that follows the actual emailed URL shape.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. No USE rows existed in the previous register to re-verify.

findings.title: Signup email-confirmation link points at the API host and 404s, blocking first login
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:182 — sign-up sets emailRedirectTo `${req.protocol}://${req.get("host")}/auth/callback`, i.e. the API origin
infra/digitalocean/Caddyfile.prod:19-30 — api.<domain> proxies every path to api:4000; only the web app (app./www.) serves /auth/callback
apps/api/src/middleware/not-found.ts:3-5 — unknown API paths return 404 JSON, so the confirmation link cannot complete
.github/workflows/deploy-do.yml:333 — production NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=https://<api_domain> confirms web and API are different hosts
apps/web/app/auth/callback/route.ts:8-15 — the working callback lives on the web host
findings.impact: New signups receive a confirmation link that dead-ends on the API 404; they cannot verify their email, so the onboarding funnel stops after the signup form. This also silently breaks the pending-approval flow that the signup copy promises.
findings.recommendation: Build emailRedirectTo from APP_BASE_URL (as forgot-password already does via resolveTrustedRedirectOrigin) so it targets the web /auth/callback. Verify the Supabase redirect allow-list contains that URL.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. External Supabase redirect allow-list config is unknown; if the URL is not allow-listed GoTrue falls back to the dashboard Site URL, but the in-repo contract is wrong either way.

findings.title: Admin approval queue cannot approve or reject memberships (roleId sent as empty string)
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/approvals/actions.ts:28-39 — approveMembership sends `{ roleId: "", status: "approved" }`
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/approvals/actions.ts:41-52 — rejectMembership sends `{ roleId: "", status: "rejected" }`
apps/api/src/validators/membership.ts:3-8 — updateMembershipSchema requires roleId: z.string().uuid(), so an empty string fails validation
apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:123-127 — PATCH /memberships/:id parses the body with that schema
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/approvals/page.tsx:116-124 — the queue renders Approve/Reject User buttons wired to those actions with no error handling
findings.impact: The single most important admin onboarding step (approving a pending user so they can enter the portal) fails: the action throws, no membership changes, and the admin sees an error screen instead of a confirmation. Pending users stay locked out until someone edits the membership from the user detail page.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the membership's current role (or make roleId optional in the PATCH schema) and return/display the API error; add a test that approval from the queue transitions status to approved.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. UI presentation of the thrown action (error boundary vs. inline) is inferred; the API rejection is certain.

findings.title: Every SDK delete reports failure after succeeding because the client cannot parse empty 204 bodies
evidence: packages/sdk/src/client.ts:96 — executeFetch unconditionally does `await res.json()` before checking res.status

apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:597, apps/api/src/routes/api-keys.ts:173, apps/api/src/routes/memberships.ts:173, apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:521 — delete handlers end with `res.status(204).send()` (46 occurrences across apps/api/src/routes/*.ts)
packages/sdk/src/__tests__/sdk-expanded.test.ts:14-40 — the test double returns a JSON body even for status 204, so CI never reproduces the real empty-body behavior
apps/web/components/admin/AdminApiKeysClient.tsx:74-84 — on the resulting parse error the UI shows 'Failed to delete API key' and keeps the row
apps/web/components/admin/RecordDetail.tsx:56-68 — module record deletes surface the raw error string
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/documents/page.tsx:438-470 — bulk delete swallows each per-item error and returns ok:true, so a real failure is indistinguishable from success
findings.impact: Deleting an API key, document, membership, webhook, module record, etc. appears to fail (error toast/raw JSON error, row stays/rolls back) even though the server deleted it; users retry, and stale rows persist until a manual refresh. Combined with the bulk loop that swallows errors, some bulk deletes claim success while single deletes claim failure — the same operation gives contradictory feedback.
findings.recommendation: In executeFetch, treat 204/empty bodies as `null` (e.g. check status 204 or content-length 0 before res.json()). Add SDK tests with truly empty bodies, and have the web delete actions surface per-item results.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Cross-cutting with domain 08 (API contracts); no existing finding covers it.

findings.title: Bulk document operations report success without per-item results (false success on partial failure)
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/documents/page.tsx:438-470 — bulkDeleteAction loops `api.documents.remove(id)` inside try/catch that ignores every error, then returns `{ok:true, ids}`
apps/web/components/admin/AdminDocumentsCenterClient.tsx:851-869 — on ok it announces 'N documents were removed.' with no per-item detail
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/documents/bulk-actions.ts:12-25 — bulk folder/metadata return `updated: documentIds.length` regardless of the API result
packages/sdk/src/documents.ts:103-120 — SDK types bulk responses as `{updated:number}` and discards the API's `{results, successful, failed}`
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:676-694 and 722-745 — the API does return per-row `results`, `successful`, `failed`
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/page.tsx:63-95 — bulk ticket update surfaces `failed` but ignores the API's `skipped` count (not in the SDK type)
findings.impact: Admins can be told 'N documents were removed/updated' when some or all items were rejected (version conflict, permission, tenant filter); the misleading success blocks retries and hides data-governance mistakes. This is the exact 'single success message over partially failed items' anti-pattern.
findings.recommendation: Plumb the API's per-item results through the SDK and web actions; render 'X succeeded, Y failed' with the failed ids/errors, and never report the requested count as the result.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Ticket lists and dashboard counts silently stop at 25 rows (no pagination) in portal and admin
evidence: apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/page.tsx:56 — api.tickets.list({ organizationId }) with no limit/page
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:98 — the API default limit is 25 (max 100)
apps/web/components/portal/SupportCenterClient.tsx:181-191 — 'Open/Closed/All Tickets' cards count only the fetched page
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/page.tsx:109-114 — api.tickets.list({}) with no pagination
apps/web/components/admin/AdminTicketCenterClient.tsx:376-382 — client-side 'Show more' only reveals rows already fetched, so it can never exceed 25
findings.impact: A client or admin with more than 25 tickets sees wrong totals and cannot reach older tickets from the list; 'All Tickets' and the open/closed metrics understate reality, and a closed ticket may be invisible. MSP staff may believe a ticket does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Paginate the list endpoints (page/limit + total) in both ticket centers, or fetch with limit=100 and add server-side paging; derive the stat cards from the API total.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Admin 'Delete Ticket' only closes the ticket; copy promises a restorable soft-delete and Restore is unreachable
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/actions.ts:79-101 — deleteTicketAction validates the typed DELETE then calls api.tickets.update(ticketId, { status: 'closed' })
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx:259-299 — the confirmation says 'This performs a safer soft-delete so the ticket can be restored later'
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx:241-252 — Restore Ticket renders only when isDeletedTicket(ticket) is true, which the delete path never sets
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/actions.ts:122-136 — restoreTicketAction only flips status back to 'new'
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:492-529 — the hard DELETE /tickets/:id endpoint exists but is never called from the web UI
findings.impact: Admins believe they deleted a ticket when they only closed it; closed tickets remain in lists/exports and count against closed-ticket stats. The promised restore path can never appear, and a genuinely deleted (API-level) ticket would have no UI recovery path.
findings.recommendation: Either call the DELETE endpoint behind the typed confirmation and implement a real tombstone/restore, or relabel the action 'Close ticket' and drop the soft-delete copy.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Related but distinct from domain 26's 'Destructive deletes are inconsistently confirmation-gated'.

findings.title: Ticket notification deep links 404 in the portal (/portal/tickets/* does not exist)
evidence: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:187-192 — tickets map to `${basePath}/tickets/${module_id}`; the portal layout passes basePath='/portal'
apps/web/components/NotificationsPageClient.tsx:94-100 — same mapping on the notifications page
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/[ticketId]/page.tsx — the real portal ticket route is /portal/support/<id>
`ls apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/tickets` → no such directory; no rewrite for /portal/tickets in apps/web/next.config.mjs:23-31
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/not-found.tsx — the 404 page is what the user lands on
findings.impact: Clicking a ticket notification — the primary action for a new ticket event — takes the client to a 404 instead of the ticket. Clients must navigate manually, and may conclude the portal is broken.
findings.recommendation: Map portal ticket notifications to /portal/support/<id> (admin keeps /admin/tickets/<id>), and add a link-resolution test for each module.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Notification surfaces swallow failures: preferences save silently fails and a failed list load renders a false empty state
evidence: apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/notifications/preferences/NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:89-96 — updatePreferences failure is caught and ignored; the success banner is the only feedback and never appears on failure
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/notifications/preferences/NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:44-52 — the initial load failure is also ignored, so toggles render as all-on defaults
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/notifications/preferences/NotificationPreferencesClient.tsx:172-176 — copy says 'Preferences are saved immediately' while the page requires Save Preferences
apps/web/components/NotificationsPageClient.tsx:60-74 — list load failure is swallowed, then line 166-167 shows 'No notifications found.'
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:175-185 — bell preference toggle reverts silently on failure (no message)
findings.impact: Users believe they disabled email notifications when the save failed, or believe they have no notifications when the API is down. Both are trust-damaging and, for preferences, can lead to missed ticket/billing email they explicitly tried to keep.
findings.recommendation: Show an inline error + retry on load and save failure; only show the empty state when the load succeeded; align the copy with the save-button model.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. NOTIF-P1-001 (preference enforcement) was re-verified fixed at 9c0b88c and is owned by domain 30; this finding is only about the UI feedback.

findings.title: NotificationBell SSE fallback leaks a 30-second polling interval per component instance
evidence: apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:108-113 — es.onerror closes the stream, starts `setInterval(fetchUnread, 30000)`, and 'returns' a cleanup that is discarded
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:115-118 — the effect cleanup only calls es.close(), never clearInterval
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:204 and app/(admin)/admin/layout.tsx:161 — the bell is mounted in both portal and admin headers
findings.impact: After any SSE failure (proxy restart, auth expiry, network blip) each mounted bell keeps polling /notifications/unread-count forever, even after unmount; repeated navigation accumulates intervals, increasing API load and the chance of rate-limit errors that further degrade the notification UI.
findings.recommendation: Store the interval id in a ref and clear it in the effect cleanup (and before starting a new one); or replace SSE with a reconnect-with-backoff + single poller.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Client-onboarding create swallows the redirect: success shows a cryptic error and invites duplicate records
evidence: apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/actions.ts:14-40 — redirect(`/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/${created.id}`) is inside try/catch; the catch returns `{ok:false, error: e.message}` where message is 'NEXT_REDIRECT'
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/new/OnboardingCreateForm.tsx:14-17 — the client renders the returned error and stays on the form
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/actions.ts:31-34 — other actions in the repo explicitly rethrow NEXT_REDIRECT, confirming the intended pattern
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/actions.ts:15-35 — the record is created before the redirect, so the data exists despite the error
findings.impact: The user is told creation failed after it succeeded, sees a meaningless 'NEXT_REDIRECT' message, and may submit again, creating duplicate onboarding records that then need manual cleanup.
findings.recommendation: Rethrow redirect errors (or move redirect outside the try/catch) as done elsewhere; add a test that asserts navigation after create.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Onboarding checklist items cannot be completed anywhere in the web app
evidence: apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/[id]/page.tsx:99-105 — checklist checkboxes are rendered `disabled`; the page has no update controls
packages/sdk/src/client-onboarding-command-center.api.ts:92-99 — updateChecklistItem exists in the SDK
apps/api/src/routes/client-onboarding-command-center.ts:242-256 — PATCH /:id/checklist/:itemId exists on the API
grep 'updateChecklistItem|checklist' apps/web/app apps/web/components apps/web/lib → no caller in the web app
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/onboarding/[id]/page.tsx:47-81 — the admin detail edits record fields but shows no checklist
findings.impact: The onboarding command center's core workflow (completing discovery/M365/security checklist items) dead-ends: items render but no user can mark them done, so progress percentages never advance and the tracker stays empty until someone updates the database directly.
findings.recommendation: Wire the checklist PATCH into the portal/admin onboarding detail (checkbox + notes + completed_by), or seed items and provide an admin completion control.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Session/MFA expiry has no user-facing explanation and the ?mfa=required step-up redirect is ignored
evidence: apps/web/middleware.ts:134-138 — expired/missing session redirects straight to /login with no reason parameter
apps/web/app/(public)/login/page.tsx — no 'session expired' copy or query-param handling (grep 'expired' → only MFA pending message)
apps/web/app/(portal)/layout.tsx:100-103 and app/(admin)/admin/layout.tsx:118-122 — MFA_REQUIRED redirects to /portal/profile/security?mfa=required
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/profile/security/page.tsx:12-17 — the page reads only `recovered`, not `mfa=required`
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/profile/security/MfaSettingsClient.tsx:100-110,166-172 — the step-up prompt appears only when generating/revoking recovery codes
findings.impact: Users bounced mid-task cannot tell whether they were signed out, blocked by permissions, or need a second factor. MFA-enforced users land on the security page with no explanation and no visible way to satisfy the requirement, effectively dead-ending the session until they discover the recovery-code flow.
findings.recommendation: Add ?reason=expired copy on /login and a visible 'Verify to continue' step-up banner (challenge+verify for any verified factor) when ?mfa=required is present.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Privileged membership/approval actions lack confirmation and success feedback (suspend/reject are one click)
evidence: apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/approvals/page.tsx:71-79 — Approve Org / Reject Org submit immediately, no confirmation
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/approvals/page.tsx:116-124 — Approve User / Reject User submit immediately, no confirmation
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/users/[userId]/page.tsx:167-233 — membership role and status (including suspended/rejected) change on Save with no confirmation dialog or result message
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/users/[userId]/actions.ts:22-50 — updateMembership has no try/catch and returns no result, so failures surface as an error boundary
apps/web/components/admin/ConfirmDialog.tsx — an accessible confirm dialog exists and is used for deletes/API keys, so the pattern is available
findings.impact: A single misclick can deny a user's access (reject/suspend) with no undo and no explicit confirmation; admins also get no 'saved' feedback, so they may repeat the action or assume it failed.
findings.recommendation: Use ConfirmDialog for status transitions that remove access, and return a success/error result rendered as a toast or inline message.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Overlaps thematically with domain 26's destructive-action rows but is a distinct (membership/access) workflow.

findings.title: Change Password form collects a Current Password it never checks and advertises a weaker rule than the API enforces
evidence: apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/profile/ProfileClient.tsx:243-256 — the Current Password field is required and bound to pwCurrent
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/profile/ProfileClient.tsx:74-98 — handlePasswordChange never sends or verifies pwCurrent; it calls auth.resetPassword(email, pwNew)
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/profile/ProfileClient.tsx:80-82,268 — client-side rule is 'at least 6 characters'
apps/api/src/routes/auth.ts:61-69 — the API requires zxcvbn score >= 3 (strong), not 6 characters
apps/web/app/(public)/signup/page.tsx:82-98 — signup shows no password requirements at all
findings.impact: Users type their current password into a field that has no effect (false security affordance), and passwords that pass the client rule are rejected by the API with a strength message the UI never explained — friction and support tickets during account setup and rotation.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused field or actually verify it (Supabase reauth), display the real strength rules up front, and reuse one shared password-policy component on signup/reset/profile.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. The 'current password not verified' aspect may also interest the security domain.

findings.title: Portal ticket creation gives no success confirmation and the tested action is dead code with a mismatched field name
evidence: apps/web/components/portal/SupportCenterClient.tsx:245-258 — on ok the modal closes silently; no toast or confirmation
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/actions.ts:7-39 — createPortalTicket reads formData 'title' and is not imported by any page (grep: only tests)
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/support/page.tsx:21-54 — the live inline action reads 'subject', matching the form field
apps/web/__tests__/app/(portal)/portal/support/actions.test.ts — covers only the dead action, so the live path has no test
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/dashboard/page.tsx:121-132 — 'Create Ticket' links to /portal/support without opening the create modal
findings.impact: Users cannot tell whether their ticket was submitted (they only notice the modal closing); the duplicate/mismatched action plus tests create a false sense of coverage, and the dashboard CTA adds an extra step.
findings.recommendation: Show a success toast with a link to the new ticket, delete the dead action (or align names), test the live action, and deep-link the dashboard CTA to an open create form.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Offline/poor-network support is absent from the running app (service worker never registered)
evidence: apps/web/public/sw.js:1-47 — a cache-first service worker exists with an 'Offline' 503 fallback
grep 'serviceWorker' apps/web/app apps/web/components apps/web/lib apps/web/instrumentation-client.ts → 0 matches, so sw.js is never registered
grep 'navigator.onLine' across the web app → 0 matches; no offline banner or retry affordance
apps/web/components/NotificationBell.tsx:42-45, apps/web/components/NotificationsPageClient.tsx:70-72 — network failures are swallowed rather than surfaced
findings.impact: On flaky connections users get silent stale/empty screens (or a generic error boundary) with no indication they are offline and no cached shell; the intended PWA caching never activates.
findings.recommendation: Register the service worker behind an env flag with a versioned cache, and add an online/offline banner plus a manual retry; or remove sw.js if offline is out of scope.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. May overlap domain 17 (mobile/PWA); not yet reported there.

findings.title: Document version history is display-only: no per-version download/restore and it hides itself for single-version documents
evidence: apps/web/components/portal/DocumentVersionsClient.tsx:36-37 — returns null when versions.length <= 1
apps/web/components/portal/DocumentVersionsClient.tsx:22-30 — load errors go to console only, then render as 'no versions'
apps/web/components/portal/DocumentVersionsClient.tsx:44-54 — rows show only version number + date, no actions
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:813-846 — the API exposes GET /:id/versions/:versionId/signed-url
packages/sdk/src/documents.ts:122-137 — the SDK has no method for that signed URL, so the UI cannot call it
findings.impact: When a document is replaced, users can see that versions exist but cannot retrieve an earlier one; a single-version document shows no version information at all, and load failures look like 'no history'.
findings.recommendation: Add a per-version download (SDK method + UI action) and an inline error state; show the version section even for one version.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

findings.title: Web edit flows never send If-Match, so concurrent admin edits silently overwrite each other
evidence: apps/api/src/middleware/optimistic-locking.ts:12-16 — requireIfMatch passes when the header is absent, making conflict detection opt-in
grep 'If-Match' packages/sdk/src → 0 matches; api.tickets.update and api.documents.update send only a JSON body
apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/actions.ts:8-35 — the edit form submits title/description/status without any version
apps/api/src/routes/tickets.ts:251-268 — the API only throws VERSION_CONFLICT when ifMatchVersion is supplied
findings.impact: Two admins editing the same ticket (or document metadata) get last-write-wins with no warning; the first admin's changes vanish, and the 409 path the API implements is never exercised by the product.
findings.recommendation: Thread the row version into edit forms and send If-Match; render the API's 409 as 'modified by someone else — reload'.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d. Impact is plausible but not reproduced (no live app run).

findings.title: Form error handling is lossy or missing: signup can hang, onboarding errors are generic, bulk invite says 'Request failed'
evidence: apps/web/app/(public)/signup/page.tsx:15-31 — signupAction is awaited with no try/catch; a thrown action leaves loading=true forever ('Creating Account...')
apps/web/app/(public)/login/page.tsx:52-57 — login wraps the same pattern in try/catch, showing the intended handling
apps/web/components/admin/OrganizationOnboardingWizard.tsx:129-131 — the catch replaces the API message with 'Onboarding failed. The slug may already be in use or the admin email is invalid.'
apps/web/components/admin/BulkInviteForm.tsx:41-43 — a request failure renders a single synthetic row with 'Request failed'
apps/web/app/(portal)/portal/client-onboarding-command-center/actions.ts:38-40 — surfaces the raw 'NEXT_REDIRECT' string
findings.impact: Users cannot distinguish validation problems (slug taken, weak password, invalid email) from outages, and the signup button can stick in a loading state with no recovery other than a reload.
findings.recommendation: Wrap all submit handlers in try/finally, keep the API's message where it is user-safe, and map validation errors to the offending field.
findings.note: Fresh finding at 8d299b8d.

report:
# Usability and Workflow Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `mainecybertech` (target `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`, read-only)
- Branch: `main`
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd`
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: domain subagent (`04_usability_workflow_audit`, area `USE`)
- Area code: USE
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/04_usability_workflow_audit.md`
- Scope limitations: static review of the code only; the app was **not** run (no server, no browser, no
  database). Claims about runtime behavior are derived from code paths and are marked with confidence.
  Supabase dashboard configuration (redirect allow-lists, SMTP) is external and unknown.

## Scope

Reviewed end-to-end web workflows in `apps/web` (Next.js App Router) against `apps/api`, `packages/sdk`,
and `infra/digitalocean` where the workflow depends on them:

- Onboarding: signup, email confirmation, pending approval, admin approval queue, organization
  onboarding wizard, client-onboarding command center.
- Login/signup/reset: password login, MFA challenge/recovery/step-up, forgot/reset password.
- Navigation: portal/admin sidebars, subnav, breadcrumbs, org switcher, global search.
- Dashboards: portal dashboard (admin dashboard inspected for structure).
- Forms: auth forms, profile, support ticket, admin module CRUD, bulk invite, onboarding wizard.
- Search/filter/sort: admin tickets, admin users, portal global search, notifications filters.
- Bulk workflows: bulk invite, bulk ticket update, bulk document folder/metadata/delete/visibility.
- Admin/support workflows: ticket lifecycle (create/triage/comment/edit/delete/restore), approvals,
  user/membership management, API keys, documents, onboarding.
- Notifications and preferences: bell, notifications page, notification preferences, profile.
- Error recovery, empty/loading states, destructive actions, session expiry, offline, help paths.

Not reviewed in depth: store/marketing funnels (public store checkout, quiz, quote), billing payment
flows (covered by domain 29), accessibility conformance (domain 05), mobile layout specifics (domain 17).

## Evidence Reviewed

| Evidence | Type | Why relevant | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/middleware.ts` | code | Session/expiry gate, domain routing, CSP | Non-authoritative UX gate (ARCH-P3-001) |
| `apps/web/lib/auth/auth-actions.ts` | code | Login/MFA/signup/logout actions | Signup redirect + MFA cookie handling |

## Executive Summary

The web app is a large, mostly coherent portal (319 routes) with several genuinely good UX foundations:
grouped permission-aware navigation, route-level error boundaries, skeleton loading states, an accessible
confirmation dialog, optimistic updates with rollback and toasts in the admin document center, per-item
results in the bulk-invite UI, and `DataErrorNote` to distinguish "load failed" from "no data".

The audit nevertheless found four P1 workflow breaks that a real user hits early:

1. **Account recovery is broken.** The emailed password-reset link lands on a page that cannot complete
   the reset, because the reset endpoint requires an authenticated session and the page never consumes
   the Supabase `code`/token.
2. **Signup cannot be completed.** The confirmation email redirect is built from the API host, which
   serves no `/auth/callback` route, so the link 404s.
3. **Admins cannot approve pending users.** The approval queue sends `roleId: ""`, which the API schema
   rejects (UUID required); the action throws instead of approving.
4. **Every delete looks like a failure.** The SDK calls `res.json()` on empty 204 bodies, so 46 API
   delete endpoints surface as errors even when the delete succeeded — and some bulk deletes then
   swallow the same error and claim success.

Beyond those, the recurring theme is **missing or misleading feedback**: bulk document operations
report the requested count rather than per-item results; ticket lists silently stop at 25 rows and
their stats are computed from that page; ticket "delete" is only a close while the UI promises a
restorable soft-delete; notification preferences can fail silently; notification deep links for
tickets 404; and the MFA step-up redirect is produced but never explained.

Recommended next actions: fix the four P1s this week (they are small, localized changes), then make
feedback truthful in the bulk/notification/ticket surfaces, and add E2E coverage that walks the
actual emailed-link shapes (signup confirm, password reset) — the current unit tests mock those paths
and therefore hide the breaks.

## Risks

| Risk | Severity | Likelihood | Impact | Evidence | Mitigation |

| Clients cannot recover accounts (reset) | P1 | High | Access loss, support load | Reset page + requireAuth endpoint | Fix reset code exchange |
| New signups cannot activate | P1 | High | Onboarding funnel broken | emailRedirectTo host | Use APP_BASE_URL |
| Admins cannot approve users | P1 | High | Clients locked out | roleId "" vs UUID schema | Fix payload + test |
| Delete operations appear broken | P1 | High | Confusion, duplicate work, trust loss | SDK `res.json()` on 204 | Empty-body handling |
| Silent partial failures on bulk docs | P2 | Medium | Data-governance mistakes | Bulk loops/actions | Per-item results |
| Users miss tickets beyond row 25 | P2 | High for large tenants | Missed SLAs | Default limit 25 | Pagination |
| Notification links 404 | P2 | High | Missed updates | Wrong route mapping | Fix mapping + test |
| Preferences silently fail | P2 | Medium | Missed/extra email | Swallowed catch | Error feedback |
| MFA-enforced sessions dead-end | P2 | Medium (only when MFA enabled) | Lockout until support | `?mfa=required` unused | Step-up banner |
| SSE fallback interval leak | P2 | Medium | API load, rate limits | Discarded cleanup | Ref + clear |

## Recommendations

### Immediate / Release Blocking

1. Fix the four P1s (reset token exchange, signup redirect host, approval roleId, SDK 204 handling).
2. Add regression tests for each: E2E reset-from-email, E2E confirm-from-email, API+web approval test, SDK empty-body test.

### This Week

3. Correct notification ticket deep links and add a link-resolution test per module.
4. Make bulk document/ticket actions report per-item results (surface `successful`/`failed`/`skipped`).
5. Add success/error feedback and ConfirmDialog to membership status transitions and approvals.
6. Clear the SSE polling interval on unmount.

### This Month

7. Paginate ticket lists (portal + admin) and derive counts from API totals.
8. Fix the ticket delete semantics (real delete + tombstone/restore, or relabel to Close).
9. Fix notification preferences error handling and copy; distinguish "load failed" from "empty".
10. Rethrow redirects in the client-onboarding action; wire checklist completion (portal or admin).
11. Add session-expired copy and an explicit MFA step-up banner on the security page.
12. Remove or implement the Current Password check and publish the real password policy.

### Later / Platform Evolution

13. Register the service worker (or remove it) and add online/offline messaging.
14. Thread If-Match/version through edit forms and render 409 conflicts.
15. Add per-version document download and always-visible version info.
16. Standardize form error mapping (API message → field/inline/toast) across all modules.

## Suggested Tests

- **Unit (web):** notification href mapping; SSE interval cleanup with fake timers; signup action rejection keeps button usable; client-onboarding action rethrows redirect.
- **Unit (SDK):** `executeFetch` with a 204/empty body resolves to null; delete methods do not retry on parse errors.
- **API:** PATCH membership with the approval-queue payload returns 400 today (regression), and returns 200 with a resolved role after the fix.
- **E2E (Playwright):** signup → follow confirmation URL shape → `/pending`; forgot password → follow reset URL shape (`?code=`) → new password → login; admin approve pending user; delete API key/document shows success; bulk document delete with one failing id shows partial result; ticket notification opens `/portal/support/<id>`; session expiry shows an explanation on `/login`.
- **Manual:** the 10 scenarios in Detailed Review.
- **CI:** add an integration job that runs the SDK against the real API container for one DELETE route (catches empty-body regressions).
